headline: Turn suffix and prefix matching into one trie prefix query: insert every suffix followed by a separator and the full word
statement: Implement WordFilter(words) and f(pref,suff), returning the largest zero-based word index whose word starts with pref and ends with suff. Return -1 when no word matches.
constraints: Words and queries contain lowercase English letters
intuition: Turn suffix and prefix matching into one trie prefix query: insert every suffix followed by a separator and the full word. Later words overwrite indices so each trie node remembers the largest match.
approach: For each word index and each suffix start, build suffix + separator + word.
Insert that sequence in a trie, storing the word index at every visited node.
Query suff + separator + pref; return -1 if any edge is absent.
Otherwise return the largest index stored at the last query node.
correctness: A trie path suff+separator+pref occurs for exactly those inserted sequences whose chosen suffix is suff and whose full word begins with pref. Storing indices during increasing-index insertion leaves the greatest matching index at every node. Therefore the final query node contains precisely the required answer.
bruteForce: Scan the dictionary backwards for each query and test startswith/endswith: O(N*(P+S)) per query.

complexity.explanation: Each of N words of maximum length L has L+1 suffix sequences, each O(L) long, giving O(N*L²) inserted characters and trie storage. A query follows only its P prefix letters, S suffix letters, and separator.

pitfalls: Return the largest index, even for duplicate words.
The separator must not belong to the word alphabet.
A suffix may overlap a prefix within the same word.
